scope: Research compilation from existing evidence and primary sources; no new application test, performance run, deployment or Git mutation. Historical and final outputs remain distinct.

comparison.baselineScope: Clean isolated build of the previous committed source using the same installed dependencies and current harness, rather than pretending it is the historical deployed asset build.

environment.cpuScope: Main renderer target rate4. Every Worker target receives an independent Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate command before resuming; actual acknowledgements or unsupported errors are retained per target. Unsupported Worker Emulation means preprocessing is NOT established as CPU4. Command acknowledgement alone does not establish a precise physical slowdown.
environment.timing: Cold: navigation-to-three accepted-and-drawn charts plus two RAF, including activation. Zoom: main view-start through chart-draw hook. Hover: separate request-to-accepted, request-to-DOM-commit, request-to-two-RAF-frame and browser-pointer-event-timestamp-to-frame metrics. Frame mark requires current workspace/view/hover identity and visible committed tooltips; actual source tooltip screenshots and Chrome paint traces are retained. Two RAFs establish a rendering opportunity, not physical monitor presentation. Playwright action upper bounds include automation overhead. Single-run and Compare samples are separate. Trace rendering/paint evidence is retained; draw hooks alone are not pixel proof.
environment.interactionProtocol: Two unmeasured warmups, then 30 measured range/hover pairs: overview, spike, reset, excluded-spike, single-step repeated six times. Single and Compare follow the same sequence. Range form values are source numeric steps.
environment.coldDefinition: Fresh browser context per sample, same browser process; OS disk caches are not flushed. Compare activation is a separate warm SPA measurement, not a fifth/sixth cold sample.
environment.tabMemory: Separate scripts/tab-memory.mjs OS footprint experiment; heap and typed-buffer ledger are not process footprint

cold.scope: Worst of two separately reported nearest-rank p95 results; samples are not pooled

zoom.scope: Worst of two separately reported nearest-rank p95 results; samples are not pooled

hover.scope: Worst of two separately reported nearest-rank p95 results; samples are not pooled

compareZoom.scope: Worst of two separately reported nearest-rank p95 results; samples are not pooled

compareHover.scope: Worst of two separately reported nearest-rank p95 results; samples are not pooled

comparison.scope: Full Chrome recording including frame screenshots: CPU4 main renderer, Worker throttling unsupported. Same5 cold contexts and30 range/hover pairs per workspace, original pointer timestamp and committed source DOM before two RAF callbacks. Targets use the worse of two full-recording p95 results; samples are never pooled. A separate no-recording result uses exactly the same application source. Sequential shared-machine runs are not a randomized causal study.

original.scope: Exact per-occurrence static replay with original and text-masked screenshots; computed foreground/ancestor opacity and worst actual background pixel contrast. Hidden/clipped cases retained with geometry. Not universal WCAG or human review certification.

final.scope: Exact per-occurrence static replay with original and text-masked screenshots; computed foreground/ancestor opacity and worst actual background pixel contrast. Hidden/clipped cases retained with geometry. Not universal WCAG or human review certification.

memory.scope: Windows OS process counters from the page renderer and every live dedicated Worker, each associated with a PID by its own User Timing marker in the same Chrome trace. Tab-owned private committed bytes/working set deduplicate those verified PIDs, including native allocations, not JS heap alone. SystemInfo-reported browser-process subtotals include shared browser/GPU/utility processes, are not exhaustive browser totals, and are not assigned wholly to the tab. Working-set sums may double-count shared pages. A process counter is not universal total tab/GPU memory, and is not a Chrome Task Manager screenshot. One isolated browser with one page, no personal profile; headed/headless configuration is recorded explicitly. Retiring isolates/shared infrastructure are reflected in the separately labelled process-subtotal scope. User Timing markers, Windows counters and the dump are sequential, not atomic; counter intervals and marker timestamps are retained.

environment.gc: No forced GC; deterministic:false memory dumps

canvas.scope: Same actual source-coordinate Canvas pixel assertion on correct and suppressed-drawing production builds. Raw subprocess output retained.

lighthouse.scope: Lighthouse desktop preset, its own simulation settings; separate from CPU4 before/after benchmark
